messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: SRE on-call (severity 2) - multiple customers reporting 5xx / slow connections hitting services in us-east-2. Auto-detect: high ICMPv6 'Packet too big' counts on egress; potential PMTUD/MTU issue. https://runbooks.internal/pmtroubleshoot :eyes:

maria: saw the page, I'm on it. I'm looking at edge LB metrics and packet logs.

maria: quick summary from tcpdump on edge-bgp-01: lots of ICMPv6 Type2 Fragmentation Needed messages:
```
15:03:12.345678 IP6 fe80::1 > 2001:db8::abcd: ICMP6, packet too big mtu 1280, length 1500
15:03:12.345679 IP6 client::12345 > our-backend::80: TCP 0
```

maria: seems like neighbor AZ (us-east-2b) recently had a jumbo frames change on the virtual network. Some VMs still advertising 9000 while route path MTU is 1500 -> PMTUD is failing because ICMPv6 is being filtered on the transit path.

alex: cc @cloud-noc, can you confirm if any recent overlay/mtu changes were rolled in us-east-2? Also any WG lockdowns on ICMPv6?

cloud-noc: we're seeing a config push at 02:40Z that adjusted segmentation offload and MTU to 9000 for a subset of hosts in us-east-2b to support high-throughput customers. We didn't touch firewall policies intentionally. Investigating whether a middlebox is dropping ICMPv6 Packet Too Big.

jamie: customers are reporting timeouts and 502s through our hosted API endpoints in that AZ. Support is fielding tickets with error like: "upstream read error: connection reset by peer" and curl shows stalled TLS. Repro from our side: dual-stack curl to service over IPv6 is slow, IPv4 works fine.

support-bot: Incidents queue: 23 open tickets referencing this outage, severity: mixed. Top affected customers: demo-startup (high), partner-ops (med).

maria: mitigation plan (fast): 1) stop advertising IPv6 for problematic frontends in us-east-2b (fail back to IPv4-only) 2) apply TCP MSS clamp on egress edge routers to 1280 (temporary) 3) request cloud vendor to remove jumbo MTU on transit path OR re-open ICMPv6.

alex: prefer approach (2) + (1). Changing vendor MTU could impact many tenants; safer to clamp on our edge and cut v6 on affected LB listeners.

maria: executing step 1: disabling ipv6 listeners on lb-prod-us-east-2b for the affected routes. Command in console (patch):
```
# aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:aws:elb:... --protocol HTTP --default-actions ... --no-ipv6
```
Applying to routes: /api/*, /embed/*, and /batch/* for the next 15m.

jamie: notifying support to set expectation: "We're temporarily routing traffic over IPv4 while we remediate underlying IPv6 path issues. No data loss expected; some latency improvements likely after the change."

maria: step 2: applying MSS clamp on edge routers (BGP-egress-01/02). Patch: ``iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu``. Doing it on the egress interfaces now.

alex: are we confident this won't break legitimate jumbo frame internal flows? Only on egress to public IPv6, right?

maria: yes, only on public egress chains. internal overlay remains untouched. I pushed the rule to the fleet with the usual rollout script: `./deploy-net-rule --target=egress --rule=mss-clamp --roll 5m`.

cloud-noc: vendor update: they found an intermediate router intentionally rate-limiting ICMPv6 for ICMP packet types > certain size on that transit segment (misconfigured DDoS rule). They're rolling back the ACL now. ETA ~18 minutes.

maria: seeing immediate reduction of ICMPv6 errors after the iptables clamp went out on edge-bgp-*. Dashboards: Packet too big events dropped 92% in first 3 mins. Latency on IPv6 endpoints is recovering slowly.

jamie: support: update to customers posted. Also asked to escalate demo-startup's case; they had an active demo earlier and reported failures.

support-bot: demo-startup: case #4532 annotated with maintenance. Engineer assigned: jamie.

alex: since vendor rollback is in flight, we should prepare rollback plan for our quick fixes: 1) remove MSS clamp after vendor confirms ICMPv6 is allowed end-to-end and MTU consistent 2) re-enable ipv6 listeners after validation.

maria: agreed. I'll keep MSS clamp active until vendor confirms AND we validate a clean PMTU (no Packet too big alerts) for 20 minutes. Then I'll progressively re-enable IPv6 listeners (canary 5% -> 50% -> 100%).

cloud-noc: rollback complete on vendor side: they removed the ACL blocking ICMPv6 at 15:25Z. We see TTL=64 ICMPv6 PTB back in logs but they pass end-to-end now.

maria: run PMTUD health check: ping with large payload and expect ICMPv6 PTB to be returned and path to adapt. Quick test:
```
ping -6 -s 1400 2001:db8::service
# expecting ICMPv6 Packet too big then subsequent packets adjust
```
Result: PTB returned and retransmission size negotiated.

maria: removing MSS clamp on egress now (rolling back in 2 batches). Command: `iptables -t mangle -D POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu`.

jamie: re-enabling IPv6 on 5% of listeners (canary). Monitoring error budget and 5xx rate.

maria: canary looks good for 10 mins, no uptick in PTB or 5xx. moving to 50%.

support-bot: update posted to status.redwood.ai: "Partial degradation affecting IPv6 endpoints in us-east-2 resolved. Some customers may have experienced transient errors; we mitigated by temporarily clamping MSS and rolling listeners back to IPv4 while vendor fixed ICMPv6 filtering. Root cause: vendor ACL blocked ICMPv6 Packet Too Big messages on a transit link during an MTU change."

alex: handoff time. I'm stepping in for the post-incident follow-up. Maria — please capture timeline, diffs, and the specific hosts affected. I'll own the RCA and vendor engagement.

maria: timeline notes:
- 14:40Z vendor MTU change rolled affecting us-east-2b transit
- 15:03Z alerts triggered: elevated ICMPv6 PTB and customer errors
- 15:06Z MSS-clamp deployed on egress (mitigated client impact)
- 15:10Z disabled IPv6 listeners on affected LB routes (reduced failed sessions)
- 15:25Z vendor rollback of ICMPv6 ACL; validated PMTUD recovery
- 15:45Z full re-enable and monitoring green

maria: I'll attach packet captures and the exact iptables diff to the incident doc in #incidents-postmortems.

alex: next steps for RCA: 1) vendor to explain why ACL pushed with ICMPv6 deny during MTU change 2) add automated PMTUD synthetic checks across regions to detect broken ICMPv6 early 3) make MSS-clamp auto-trigger in runbook when PTB rate spikes 4) consider defaulting to IPv4-only for public listeners when path MTU has not been verified.

jamie: support follow-up: will reach out to top impacted customers with a post-incident note and offer to review any replay data they saw.

cloud-noc: we will add vendor SLA note to require notification for MTU changes and confirm ICMPv6 reachability.

maria: handing off to alex for RCA and postmortem. I'll stay reachable for any questions.

alex: thanks team. Closing active mitigation. I'll open a formal incident ticket and schedule RCA meeting for tomorrow 10:00AM PT.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to S3 — monitoring.

maria: ack.

jamie: thanks everyone :heart:

support-bot: Tickets updated and customers notified.
